mainEntity.name: Is it cheaper to automate or to hire in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the task mix, not the job title. A mostly deterministic role — intake, scheduling, reconciliation, follow-up — usually costs less to automate than to staff at Michigan's fully loaded rates. A mostly judgment role is cheaper to hire, because the automation fails at exactly the part that matters.

mainEntity.name: What is the fully loaded cost of an employee in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the salary by roughly 1.4. BLS data for March 2026 shows benefits at 30.1% of private-industry total compensation, which is a 43% load on wages. For a $41,100 medical secretary that is about $58,800 a year before recruiting or turnover.

mainEntity.name: Will AI replace my receptionist or bookkeeper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Probably not the role — likely part of the task list. The repeatable portion can move to a system; the judgment, the relationship, and the accountability cannot. Most small businesses using AI actually grew headcount over the past year, so treat this as a capacity question first.

mainEntity.name: Can I just use a cloud AI tool for client data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not if the data is protected health information, privileged, or proprietary. The objection is that the data leaves your building, and no agreement changes that. A Local LLM running on-premises delivers the productivity without the exposure — which is what makes HIPAA-ready AI documentable.

mainEntity.name: Do I need blockchain to verify an automated workflow?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need independent verification. Blockchain is how you get it without trusting a single party's database: if the record is tamper-evident and independently checkable, the mechanism matters less than the guarantee. Where a workflow touches money or compliance, that guarantee is the difference between a log and evidence.

The process with the highest volume, the clearest definition, and the lowest cost of being wrong. Define and measure it before you automate it — undefined ROI and bad input data are the two leading reasons automation projects get abandoned, and both are fixable before you spend anything.
